newsitem.title: USA: Mitchell Energy to buy oil, gas assets.
newsitem.headline: Mitchell Energy to buy oil, gas assets.

text.p: Mitchell Energy & Development Corp on Wednesday said it would use money from the sale of its Woodlands Corp real estate venture to buy more oil and gas assets.
The company currently has nine outstanding offers to buy assets and is "actively working ideas on 35 others," its chairman, George Mitchell, said at the company's annual meeting.
Mitchell President Bill Stevens said the assets to be purchased include both oil and gas production properties and facilities for the company's gas services business.

He also said the company was heartened by its recent victory in a lawsuit filed by a group that said Mitchell Energy's oil and gas operations in north Texas had polluted water wells. An earlier suit making the same charge ended in a $204 million judgment against the company and is currently on appeal.

"The (latest) verdict reinforces our belief that we will eventually be vindicated in the (first) case as well. We're hopeful that the appeals court will either throw out the judgment altogether or at least reduce the amount of the damages dramatically," Mitchell said.
"Hopefully by this time next year the north Texas litigation will be ancient history," he said.

By August the company expects to close on the sale of the Woodlands, a large multi-use development north of Houston, to a partnership of Crescent Real Estate Equities Co and Morgan Stanley Real Estate Fund. The sale is expected to net Mitchell Energy $460 million.
Along with asset purchases, "other possible uses for some of the proceeds include buying back some of our stock, paying down debt or even paying a special dividend to shareholders," Mitchell said.
The Houston-based company had earnings of $103 million, or $1.99 a share, on revenues of $1.1 billion in 1996.
